verdicts.claim: By default SQLite auto-checkpoints on the COMMIT that makes the WAL 1000 pages or more (about 4 MB). It also checkpoints when the last connection closes
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages'; 'about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB'; '1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection ... closes'

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE copies as many frames as it can without waiting for readers or writers. It can leave the checkpoint unfinished. It never invokes the busy handler
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode ... might leave the checkpoint unfinished'

verdicts.claim: FULL waits, invoking the busy handler, until no writer is active and all readers use the most recent snapshot... blocks new writers, but not new readers
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded'

verdicts.claim: Checkpoints are mutually exclusive across processes. If another process is already running a checkpoint, the call fails with SQLITE_BUSY, and the busy handler is not invoked
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked'

verdicts.claim: FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE also take the writer lock and retry it under the busy handler; if the handler gives up, the call finishes as PASSIVE and returns SQLITE_BUSY
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case'

verdicts.claim: sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() writes pnLog/pnCkpt; both -1 on error or non-WAL; after a successful TRUNCATE both are 0
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE ... both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA journal_size_limit=N truncates a WAL larger than N bytes back to N at each commit and WAL reset. Default -1 (no limit). Zero truncates to minimum
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'Each time a transaction is committed or a WAL file resets ... truncated to the limit'; 'A negative number implies no limit'; 'set the journal_size_limit to zero' (default -1 not quoted in excerpt read, but negative=no limit stated)

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns one row with three integers. Column 1 (busy) is 1 when a RESTART, FULL or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'single row with three integer columns. The first column is usually 0 but will be 1 if a RESTART or FULL or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked'

verdicts.claim: sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(db, N) changes threshold at run time; zero or negative turns automatic checkpoints off; checkpoints are PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely'; 'Checkpoints initiated by this mechanism are PASSIVE'

verdicts.claim: Litestream v0.5.x: truncate-page-n defaults to 121359 pages (~500 MB) ... min-checkpoint-page-count 1000 (~4 MB) ... checkpoint-interval 1 minute, after each sync in order
verdicts.evidence: guide: 'evaluated in this order after each sync'; 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default : ~500MB'; 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000 # Default : ~4MB'; 'checkpoint-interval: 1m'

verdicts.claim: Litestream removed max-checkpoint-page-count in v0.5.0 because of safety concerns with RESTART checkpoints. truncate-page-n replaces it
verdicts.evidence: config: 'The max-checkpoint-page-count field has been removed in v0.5.0 due to safety concerns with RESTART checkpoints. Use truncate-page-n instead.'

verdicts.claim: Litestream takes over checkpointing. It starts a long-running read transaction so no other process can checkpoint or restart the WAL
verdicts.evidence: how-it-works: 'taking over the checkpointing process. It starts a long-running read transaction to prevent any other process from checkpointing'

verdicts.claim: SQLite docs say the 1000-page default seems to work well in test applications on workstations
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'reaches 1000 pages and this strategy seems to work well in test applications on' workstations

verdicts.claim: If at least one reader is always active, no checkpoint can complete, and the WAL grows without bound. A Syncthing thread posted 2026-02-06 describes the same
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound'; forum post dated February 6, 2026

verdicts.claim: Tailscale recorded 19 corruption incidents over six months, starting in August 2025, before it found the cause
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: 'In total, we faced 19 separate instances of database corruption over six months'; Register: 'in August 2025 those backups began detecting database corruption'

verdicts.claim: In two incidents, a committed write was invisible to later transactions, with no error raised
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: 'In two incidents ... data written and committed by one transaction was inexplicably invisible to later transactions ... without raising an error'

verdicts.claim: WAL-reset bug likely present 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09); fixed in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13); backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §11: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'

verdicts.claim: The 3.51.3 and 3.53.0 release logs both list the fix
verdicts.evidence: Both logs: 'Fix the WAL-reset database corruption bug'; 3.53.0 dated 2026-04-09

verdicts.claim: Tailscale says the fix first shipped in 3.52.0; release log lists 3.52.0 (2026-03-06) as Withdrawn, features moved to 3.53.0; rounding change caused false corruption warnings
verdicts.evidence: 3.52.0 log: 'Withdrawn ... moved forward into version 3.53.0'; Tailscale: 'Because this change caused false corruption warnings, the SQLite developers withdrew the 3.52.0 release and instead published 3.51.3'

verdicts.claim: SQLite developer Dan found and fixed it on 2026-03-03, per SQLite's WAL page
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'On 2026-03-03, one of the SQLite developers (Dan) found and fixed a bug'

verdicts.claim: SQLite says the occurrence rate appears at or below SSD malfunctions or cosmic-ray hits; Canonical says real-world impact is very low
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'less than or equal to the expected occurrence rate of SSD malfunctions and/or cosmic-ray hits'; Canonical: 'its real-world impact (which is very low)'

verdicts.claim: Aggressive manual checkpointing raises exposure; Tailscale took manual control and checkpointed very aggressively
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: 'more likely to hit the bug ... we take manual control of the checkpointing process, and we checkpoint very aggressively'; wal.html: 'requires an unusual usage pattern'

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: wal.html says the bug was found and fixed 2026-03-03; Canonical says SQLite disclosed and published the fix on March 5, 2026
verdicts.evidence: Canonical: 'On March 5, 2026 SQLite disclosed the bug and published a fix'

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: Litestream says a passive checkpoint returns SQLITE_BUSY when readers or writers are active
verdicts.evidence: guide: 'Non-blocking—returns SQLITE_BUSY if readers or writers are active ... logging "passive checkpoint skipped"'
